physical.notes: Cabinet sheet 7SW75 ADVANCE on the coin door, wired GRN to CPU connector 1J4-3 (7P1-5, 7P2-14). PinMAME constant S6_SWADVANCE, sampled into the display PIA's CA1. Steps the bookkeeping functions, adjustments and diagnostic tests with Auto-Up/Manual-Down; the harness pressed it to walk Tests 01-03.

Cabinet sheet 7SW74 AUTO-UP / MANUAL-DOWN on the coin door, wired BLU to CPU connector 1J4-4 (7P1-6, 7P2-15). PinMAME constant S6_SWUPDN, sampled into the display PIA's CB1. Public 1 is Auto-Up: the retained runs enter the lamp and switch tests with 1 and the solenoid test with 0, as the booklet's procedure requires. A two-position switch has no rest state; normally_closed follows that public convention.
The DIAGNOSTIC pushbutton beside the Master Command switches (booklet Figure 2). PinMAME constant S6_SWCPUDIAG: s6.c asserts the CPU's NMI line while it is 1.

The sound board's diagnostic pushbutton: the drawing set's Special Maintenance Information says pressing it produces eight electronic sounds and then, with the Speech Module, the BLACKOUT vocabulary, repeating until the game is turned off and on. PinMAME constant S6_SWSOUNDDIAG, passed to the sound board's diagnostic input.

The MASTER COMMAND ENTER pushbutton beside the Master Command slide switches, behind the insert door (booklet page 7 and Figure 2): pressing it enters the Master Command setting and blinks the LEDs once. PinMAME constant S6_ENTER: s6_dips_r returns the Master Command bank to the ROM only while it is held.

In PinMAME a consumer cannot drive this address: INITGAMEFULL declares FLIP_SWNO(0,46), and core_updateSw copies cabinet button 82 into 46 on every update. inputs.label: Sound Board DS1 Switch 2 - Speech Enable

physical.notes: Miniature switch 2 of DS1 on the sound board. The Sound Board Logic Diagram (16D-8224) wires DS1 position 2 to the 6821 IC10's PB5 (through R2 and jumper W9), with a 4.7K pull-up, and the switch grounds the line when ON. PinMAME's S6_COMPORTS calls this bit Sound Dip 1, and wmssnd.c s67s_cmd_w copies Sound Dip 1 and 2 uninverted onto PB5 and PB6, so public 0 is ON, speech enabled and public 1 is OFF, speech inhibited; PinMAME's default is 0. The drawing set's Electrical Adjustments: 'Set miniature switch 2 to ON to enable speech; set it to OFF to inhibit speech.' Without the Speech Module its setting does not matter. The printed switch number and PinMAME's number are crossed: public DIP 1 is switch 2 and public DIP 2 is switch 1.

mechanisms.behavior: A drained ball comes to rest in the outhole on switch 9. The ball release 1 kicks it into the shooter lane, and the player plunges by hand. Start fires 1 3.80 s after the credit button (after the 3-bank resets 4 and 5), and a drain fires 4 and 5 again and then 1 1.06 s later. No transcribed page counts the balls installed; the rules have no multiball, both scripts load one ball, and the gameplay run served one ball at a time.
mechanisms.label: Outhole and ball release

mechanisms.behavior: Three drop targets below the bottom jet bumper. Each target switch is closed while its target is down; the series switch 28 tells the ROM the bank is made, and the reset 4 raises all three. In the gameplay run 4 fired at the closure of 28 and not while the three targets were down with 28 open. Making the bank lights the eject hole red lamp 45; the center 3-bank arrow lamps rotate from the spinners.
mechanisms.label: Center 3-bank drop targets

mechanisms.behavior: Three drop targets at the upper right. Series switch 36 and reset 5 as for the center bank (5 fired 0.015 s after 36 closed). Making the bank lights the eject hole yellow lamp 44, advances the top 3-bank arrow lamps, lights the right spinners and lights BLACKOUT 46.
mechanisms.label: Top 3-bank drop targets

mechanisms.behavior: Kick-out hole on the right side. Ball-presence switch 40 is closed while a ball rests in it; kicker 6 ejects it. With BLACKOUT 46 lit (eject hole green, yellow and red lit) the hole's value doubles and the special-relay sequence runs before the ball is kicked: in the gameplay run 6 fired 5.09 s after the entry. When lit for Extra Ball (the spinner loop collecting 20,000, or the five green targets while loop 20,000 is lit) it awards the Extra Ball; the booklet gives the lit Specials to the outlanes, not the eject hole.
mechanisms.label: Eject hole

mechanisms.behavior: The special relay 6L15 (solenoid 15) has a normally closed contact in series with the 6.3 VAC G.I. winding, so energizing 15 darkens the coin door, playfield and insert board G.I. In the gameplay run a ball entering the eject hole with BLACKOUT lit pulsed 15 seven times, the fourth pulse holding it 2.30 s; every lamp went out 0.09 s after the entry, lamps 1-64 then lit one by one during the long hold, the coin lockout 16 dropped at 0.08 s and returned at 4.56 s, and the eject kicker 6 fired at 5.09 s with lamps 43-46 out. Whether the sequence also runs without BLACKOUT lit was not observed. Relay timing beyond these readings and the visual fade belong to the table.
mechanisms.label: Blackout: special relay and general illumination

mechanisms.behavior: Three top rollovers 29, 30 and 31 light the "1", "2" and "3" lamps 28-30; spotting all three advances the bonus multiplier. Actuating the right flipper rotates the lit lamps (LANE CHANGE): PinMAME copies the right button 82 into 46. In the gameplay run the right button moved a lit "1" to "2" and then to "3", and the left button changed nothing.

Gameplay shows the knocker, the start sequence, the five switch-fired specials, both 3-bank resets from their series switches, the eject-hole Blackout sequence on the special relay 15, the outhole release and the ball roll tilt. No run establishes bulb quantity, physical location or mechanical timing.
